samples.summary: `Worksheet.reloadDimensions` — the documented "call this when a remote change arrives" path — reloads dimensions, styles, merges, freeze, filter, hidden and pivot state but was NOT given the new `loadSpillBlockers()` call, so the exact failure the diff fixes for undo/redo/open still happens on every collaborative sync and pivot refresh.
samples.evidence: packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:5219-5226 reloads every other cached model state after remote changes but omits `loadSpillBlockers()`. It is invoked from packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/sheet-view.tsx:1152 (`runRemoteSync` → `sheet.reloadDimensions()`, i.e. remote cell data replaced without a local calculation pass) and sheet-view.tsx:1648 (pivot refresh after `invalidateStore()`), plus lakehouse-view.tsx:123,213,266. Per the diff's own rationale in sheet.ts:1032-1039, any path that replaces cell data without recalculating leaves `spillBlockers` empty/stale while blocked anchors still exist in the store, so clearing the restored blocker never re-queues its anchor and the `#REF!` becomes permanent. Fix belongs in the new code: add `await this.sheet!.loadSpillBlockers()` after `loadMerges()` in `reloadDimensions`.

samples.summary: Row/column insert, delete and move (`shiftCells`/`moveCells`) shift every other sref-keyed cache (merges, range styles, conditional formats, validations, filter/hidden state) but never shift or rebuild `spillBlockers`, whose keys AND values are srefs — the new `loadSpillBlockers()` rebuild was not wired into these paths either.
samples.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:1401-1434 shifts rowStyles/rangeStyles/conditionalFormats/dataValidations/merges/filter/hidden, then only calls `recalculateAllFormulaCells()` (sheet.ts:1473). `spillBlockers` (sheet.ts:313) is keyed by blocker sref and valued by anchor sref; after a shift the recalculation registers new entries via `registerSpillBlocker`, but `clearSpillBlockers(newAnchorSref)` (calculator.ts:122) cannot remove entries recorded under the anchor's OLD sref, so a stale registration survives. Consequence: clearing an unrelated cell re-queues an anchor that no longer lives there, or the real blocker's removal never frees the anchor and the `#REF!` sticks — the same class of bug the diff's rebuild addresses. `loadSpillBlockers()` after the shift would fix it.

samples.summary: `ReadonlyStore.getFormulaGrid()` returns an empty map, so `loadSpillBlockers()` is a silent no-op for read-only/preview surfaces — the new "blocker map is derivable from the store" invariant does not hold for that store implementation.
samples.evidence: packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts:153-155 `async getFormulaGrid(): Promise<Grid> { return new Map(); }`. The new `loadSpillBlockers` (sheet.ts:1039-1050) derives the map solely from `store.getFormulaGrid()`, so on this store it always yields an empty map. Low impact today because the store forbids mutation, but any future edit path over a ReadonlyStore-backed sheet silently loses blocker registrations, and tests exercising it will not reproduce production behaviour.

samples.summary: The shared concurrency test harness mirrors `Worksheet.initialize`'s load sequence but was not updated with `loadSpillBlockers()`, so every concurrency test now boots a sheet in a state production never has.

samples.summary: `loadSpillBlockers()` on every undo and redo walks the entire formula grid (a full worksheet scan in the Yorkie store) plus an awaited per-cell `store.get` over each blocked footprint, putting an O(all formula cells) pass on a hot keystroke path.
samples.evidence: sheet.ts:1039-1050 iterates `await this.store.getFormulaGrid()`; the Yorkie implementation (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:549-558) iterates every worksheet entry to build it. The new calls at sheet.ts:5103 and sheet.ts:5140 run this on each undo/redo, and `findSpillBlocker` (sheet.ts:1011-1029) then awaits `getCell` per footprint cell. samples.summary: The new rule that a merged block blocks a spill changes the meaning of already-stored documents (ghosts written under a merge before this change), and no load-time reconciliation removes those now-illegal ghosts — they keep rendering until something happens to re-evaluate their anchor.
samples.evidence: findSpillBlocker (sheet.ts:1021) now returns a blocker for any footprint cell inside a merge, but `loadSpillBlockers` (sheet.ts:1039) only records registrations for anchors already flagged `spillBlocked` in the store; a legacy anchor that successfully spilled under a merge is left with live ghosts under the block and no recalculation is queued at load, so old docs sit in a state the new rule says is impossible. A migration/reconcile pass (or recalculating such anchors during `loadSpillBlockers`) would close it.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `Worksheet.reloadDimensions` (packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:5219-5242) — documented as the "call this when a remote change arrives" entry point — reloads dimensions, styles, merges, freeze, filter, hidden and pivot state but never calls `loadSpillBlockers()`, unlike `initialize()` which does so at worksheet.ts:424 right after `loadMerges()`. A repo-wide grep for `loadSpillBlockers` returns only three production call sites (worksheet.ts:424, sheet.ts:5103 undo, sheet.ts:5140 redo) plus a test, and `spillBlockers` has no other rebuild path (only register/clear/consume at sheet.ts:975/983/993). The stale path is reachable: sheet-view.tsx:1278-1284 subscribes to remote-change and `remote-change-utils.ts:5-6` matches `$.sheets.*.cells`, so remote cell replacement reaches `runRemoteSync` → `reloadDimensions()` (sheet-view.tsx:1152-1153); the only follow-up, `recalculateCrossSheetFormulas()` (sheet.ts:3147-3166), early-returns unless cross-sheet refs exist and recalculates only those srefs, so local blocked anchors get no calculation pass. Per the diff's own rationale (sheet.ts:1031-1038) and the absence of any fallback in `consumeSpillBlocker` (sheet.ts:993-997, used at 1106-1107), clearing a restored blocker then never re-queues its anchor and the `#REF!` becomes permanent. Same gap on the pivot-refresh path (sheet-view.tsx:1647-1648) and lakehouse-view.tsx:123,213,266. This is squarely blast-radius: an invariant established by the new code is not maintained on a sibling entry point that other modules depend on. Major.

finding.summary: Row/column insert, delete and move (`shiftCells`/`moveCells`) shift every other sref-keyed cache (merges, range styles, conditional formats, validations, filter/hidden state) but never shift or rebuild `spillBlockers`, whose keys AND values are srefs — the new `loadSpillBlockers()` rebuild was not wired into these paths either.
finding.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:1401-1434 shifts rowStyles/rangeStyles/conditionalFormats/dataValidations/merges/filter/hidden, then only calls `recalculateAllFormulaCells()` (sheet.ts:1473). `spillBlockers` (sheet.ts:313) is keyed by blocker sref and valued by anchor sref; after a shift the recalculation registers new entries via `registerSpillBlocker`, but `clearSpillBlockers(newAnchorSref)` (calculator.ts:122) cannot remove entries recorded under the anchor's OLD sref, so a stale registration survives. Consequence: clearing an unrelated cell re-queues an anchor that no longer lives there, or the real blocker's removal never frees the anchor and the `#REF!` sticks — the same class of bug the diff's rebuild addresses. `loadSpillBlockers()` after the shift would fix it.

verdict.reason: The literal absence checks out — neither shiftCells (sheet.ts:1393-1481) nor moveCells (sheet.ts:1565-1650) shifts or rebuilds spillBlockers, and loadSpillBlockers has only three call sites (view/worksheet.ts:424, sheet.ts:5103, sheet.ts:5140), none of them in the shift/move path. But the claimed harm is already guarded by the recalculation both paths end in. shiftCells:1473 and moveCells:1643 call recalculateAllFormulaCells, which loads EVERY formula sref from the store (sheet.ts:1655-1662) and runs calculate over all of them; calculate's spill branch unconditionally re-derives the blocker via findSpillBlocker and re-registers it under the new srefs (calculator.ts:105-109) or clears it (calculator.ts:122) — this is not behind the "unchanged value" early return, which lives only in the scalar branch (calculator.ts:149-155). So after a shift every still-blocked anchor has a correct, correctly-keyed entry: no registration is missing, and the asserted "clearSpillBlockers(newAnchorSref) cannot remove entries under the old sref, so the #REF! sticks" outcome cannot occur here. The only residue is extra stale entries, and every consumer of the map (registerSpillBlocker sheet.ts:975, clearSpillBlockers sheet.ts:983, consumeSpillBlocker sheet.ts:993 with call sites at 1106, 1247, 1316, 2418, 2629, 4662) can do nothing with a stale entry but add a sref to a recalculation set; calculate skips srefs without formulas (calculator.ts:49) and re-evaluating a real formula is derived from stored state and idempotent. Worst case is a redundant recalculation and slow map growth — a minor inefficiency, not the data/consistency break claimed. The undo/redo/open cases the rebuild addresses are materially different: they replace cell data with no calculation pass at all (sheet.ts:5099-5103), which is precisely why the rebuild is needed there and not after shift/move.

finding.summary: moveRangeTo no longer overwrites destination cells at spill-ghost offsets, so pre-existing destination data survives inside the "moved" block and now blocks the anchor's re-spill
finding.evidence: movedGrid (sheet.ts:2386-2400) now skips every cell with `spillAnchor`, and `setGrid` (sheet.ts:2408 → store/memory.ts:137) only writes the keys given — it does not clear the rest of destRange. Previously the ghosts were written and clobbered whatever sat at those destination offsets. Now, if the destination holds user data at a ghost offset, calculator.ts:109 (`existing && (existing.v || existing.f) && !existing.spillAnchor`) treats it as a blocker, so the dropped array formula lands as #REF! and the stale destination value stays visible inside the block the user just dropped. The drag-move caller packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4349 does no destination-occupancy check, so this is silent. Fix belongs in the new moveRangeTo code: clear the destination cells at ghost offsets before re-evaluating the anchor.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts moveRangeTo skips ghost cells and never clears the destination cells at those ghost offsets, leaving pre-existing destination data to block the anchor's re-spill; its prescribed fix is "clear the destination cells at ghost offsets before re-evaluating the anchor." That clearing is already in the code. The ghost-skip is real (sheet.ts:2545-2549), but every skipped ghost is recorded in skippedGhosts (sheet.ts:2546 - all ghosts, not only the stale subset used for the source clear at sheet.ts:2626), and sheet.ts:2640-2647 iterates skippedGhosts, translates each sref by the move delta, and calls clearCellForOverwrite on the destination position. clearCellForOverwrite (sheet.ts:1066-1096) deletes the cell at that physical ref, records it in changedSrefs, and re-queues owning anchors / consumes blockers, so the offset is genuinely emptied. Ordering holds: that loop runs before recalculateWithUnblocked at sheet.ts:2698, so findSpillBlocker / calculator.ts:105-109 cannot see a stale destination value as a blocker. There is also no collision with the earlier setGrid(movedGrid) at sheet.ts:2567, since movedGrid keys come from non-ghost source srefs and the cleared offsets from ghost source srefs, which are disjoint sets. Additionally the finding's cited evidence lines are misattributed: sheet.ts:2386-2400 is the cut-paste stale-ghost handling, not movedGrid (built at sheet.ts:2540-2559). The drag-move caller at view/worksheet.ts:4352 does lack a destination-occupancy check, but that is immaterial because the model clears the offsets itself.

finding.summary: undo/redo never rebuild the in-memory spillBlockers map, so undoing one of the newly-consuming gestures leaves a blocked anchor permanently unregistered
finding.evidence: `Sheet.undo` (sheet.ts:4916-4945) and `redo` (sheet.ts:4950) reload dimensions/styles/merges/freeze/filter/hidden/pivot but never touch `this.spillBlockers` (declared sheet.ts:313) and never recalculate formulas. This delta makes moveRangeTo, cut-paste, mergeSelection and autofill all consume the registration (sheet.ts:2261, 2449, 2696, 4452). Undoing such a gesture restores the blocker cell from the CRDT while the registration stays consumed, so a later clear of that cell no longer re-queues the anchor and the spill stays at #REF! until an unrelated edit. To confirm: an undo test around cut-pasting a blocker cell away and then deleting it again.

verdict.reason: The core presence claim is false. `Sheet.undo` (sheet.ts:5088-5122) calls `await this.loadSpillBlockers()` at sheet.ts:5103 and `Sheet.redo` (sheet.ts:5127+) calls it at sheet.ts:5140, each with a comment stating precisely the rationale the finding says is missing. `loadSpillBlockers` (sheet.ts:1039-1051) clears the map (1040) and rebuilds it from `store.getFormulaGrid()` via `findSpillBlocker` for every cell carrying `spillBlocked`/`spillRows`/`spillCols` (1042-1049), so a registration consumed by moveRangeTo/cut-paste/mergeSelection/autofill is re-derived after the undo restores the blocker cell, and a later clear of that cell does re-queue the anchor. The finding's own cited line range (4916-4945) is `unsetRangeStyleValues`, not undo, indicating the quoted evidence was not read against this tree. No permanent-#REF! window exists on the described path.

finding.summary: mergeSelection's clearing loop deletes spill ghosts (and a covered spill anchor) without ghost cleanup or clearSpillBlockers, leaving half-written spills and orphan ghosts
finding.evidence: sheet.ts:4441-4455 deletes every non-anchor cell in the merged rect. It now consumes blocker registrations (4452) but, unlike setData (sheet.ts:1100-1119) and removeData (sheet.ts:1180-1194), it does not special-case a cell that is a spill ghost or a live spill anchor. Merging over part of a spill erases the ghosts while the anchor keeps its `spillRows`/`spillCols` (a truncated spill that only recovers on an unrelated recalculation); merging over a spill anchor deletes the formula and leaves its outside-the-merge ghosts orphaned, which setData:1095 / removeData:1173 / autofill:2692 all refuse to touch.

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. sheet.ts:4441-4455 is the tail of the border-preset routine and `toggleRangeStyle`, not a merge clearing loop. `mergeSelection` lives at sheet.ts:4589-4642 and its covered-cell loop (4612-4621) does not delete cells inline — it delegates each covered cell to `clearCellForOverwrite` (4615-4619). That helper (sheet.ts:1066-1108) performs precisely the handling the finding says is missing: a spill ghost is deleted and its owning anchor added to `requeuedAnchors` (1075-1080); a live spill anchor gets `clearSpillBlockers(sref)` (1083) and all of its ghosts deleted, including those outside the merge rect (1084-1093); a blocked anchor gets `clearSpillBlockers` (1096); and the blocker registration is consumed into `requeuedAnchors` (1106-1107). `mergeSelection` then registers the merge and calls `recalculateWithUnblocked(changedSrefs, unblockedAnchors)` (4623-4630), which seeds requeued anchors into the dependants map (1116-1131), so a covered spill is re-decided in the same batch rather than left truncated until an unrelated recalculation. Neither alleged harm (orphan ghosts, half-written spill) can occur on this path.
